lead.headline: Hot Inflation Locks In a December Fed Hike as Anthropic Opens Its Record IPO Roadshow and Oil Falls on Iran Hopes
lead.deck: October prices rose 0.4% and core 0.3%, both above forecasts, pushing December hike odds near 99%. Stocks surged Monday on cheaper oil, and Russia-Ukraine talks began in Abu Dhabi.

board_note: Figures as of Nov. 9-10 (Monday close; CPI released Tuesday); no annual CPI rate was published for October; sources in each story.

stories.headline: October Inflation Runs Hot: Prices Up 0.4% in a Month, Core 0.3%, Both Above Forecasts
stories.deck: The last big price reading before the Fed meets in December lands above what economists expected, with food and energy leading.
stories.summary: October CPI rose 0.4% (forecast 0.3%); core rose 0.3% (forecast 0.2%); no annual rate because of a data gap.
paras: The Labor Department reported that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October on a seasonally adjusted basis, after a 0.6% jump in September and above the 0.3% economists had expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3%, the same pace as August and September and a notch above the 0.2% forecast.

Food rose 0.5% (groceries 0.4%, restaurant meals 0.5%), and energy rose 0.7% after a 5.2% surge in September. Gasoline was up 1.0% after seasonal adjustment, though before adjustment pump prices fell 0.7%. Shelter rose 0.3%, with owners' equivalent rent up 0.3% and rent of a primary residence up 0.2%.

There is no headline year-over-year rate this month. The Bureau of Labor Statistics did not collect October 2025 prices during that year's government shutdown, so it left most 12-month changes blank. The few annual figures it did publish include unadjusted gasoline up 37.4%, new vehicles up 0.7% and used cars and trucks down 3.3%.
money: Groceries and restaurant meals both rose 0.5% in a month, so a weekly price-per-unit comparison across stores and store brands is worth the effort.
Higher-for-longer rate expectations tend to keep savings and money-market yields attractive; compare your account's rate against current top offers.
Variable-rate debt, such as credit cards and adjustable loans, is the part of a budget most exposed if the Fed raises rates next month, so paying those down first is a common priority.
Used-car prices were down 3.3% from a year earlier, a small bright spot for anyone shopping for a vehicle.

sources.t: Consumer Price Index News Release, October 2026 (BLS)
Inflation: CPI comes in hotter than expected (CBS News)
A hotter CPI raises odds of a December Fed rate hike (IBTimes)
US inflation set to cool in October, forecasts (Business Standard)

stories.headline: A December Fed Rate Hike Is Now Close to a Sure Thing, and a Half-Point Move Is on the Table
stories.deck: After the CPI report, futures put the odds of a quarter-point increase near 99%, and a Fed governor has said he could back double that.
stories.summary: CME odds of a December hike jumped to 98.8% from 84%; Waller has said he could favor 50 basis points.
paras: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in London that he was leaning toward raising rates in December even if October inflation had come in soft, and that he would back a half-point increase if it came in hot. According to IBTimes, he argued that moving only 25 basis points would put the Fed's credibility at risk.

CME FedWatch odds of a December hike to a 4.00%-4.25% range rose to 98.8% after the report, up from 84% before it. The Fed held its rate at 3.75%-4.00% on Oct. 28 and described inflation as elevated, with two officials favoring a hike, according to a market recap.
The central bank's next meeting is Dec. 8-9. The October CPI was described in a Bloomberg preview as the last reading before that meeting.
money: A rate hike usually lifts the yield on savings accounts and certificates of deposit within weeks; locking a CD rate before a hike can be a trade-off versus keeping cash flexible.
Credit-card APRs track the Fed's rate closely, so a larger balance carried into 2027 gets more expensive after each hike.
Mortgage rates are set by bond markets rather than directly by the Fed, which is why the 30-year rate has been falling even as hike odds rose, but they can reverse quickly.
Anyone with an adjustable-rate loan or HELOC may want to check when the next rate reset happens and by how much it could move.

stories.headline: Anthropic Launches Its IPO Roadshow: Up to 825 Million Shares at $70 to $78, Ticker ANT
stories.deck: The roadshow opened Tuesday after a leaked, wrong price range was pulled back overnight; no listing date has been announced.
stories.summary: Roadshow terms are out: $70-$78 a share on Nasdaq under ANT; base deal would raise about $64 billion at the top.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. Anthropic published the terms of its proposed offering on Nov. 10: 825,000,000 Class A shares in total, of which the company is selling 801,351,354 and existing stockholders 23,648,646, at an expected $70 to $78 a share. Underwriters hold a 30-day option on up to 123,750,000 more shares. The company has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. At $78, the base deal would be roughly $64.35 billion (825 million shares times $78).

The range follows a stumble. Late Nov. 9, an email to bankers showed about 867 million shares at $70 to $80; a second email called the pricing details inaccurate within roughly 80 minutes, according to 24/7 Wall St. Before that correction, trading had been reported as possible as soon as Nov. 19 or 20, but Anthropic's own page gives no listing date.

Context from earlier reporting: Anthropic was valued at $965 billion after a $65 billion Series H round and had an annual revenue run rate of about $47 billion as of June. Renaissance Capital wrote that the backdrop looks weaker than the company likely expected, after tech stocks fell on fears of an AI crackdown following the midterms, and that pricing could come the week of Nov. 16. Three smaller IPOs (Rezera, vVardis and Windward Bio, $175 million to $214 million each) are also slated for this week.
money: Read the final prospectus before deciding anything; the price range, share count and risk factors can change before pricing.
Whether a retail investor can buy at the IPO price depends on the broker's allocation, and most buyers get shares only after trading starts, often at a different price.
Many broad index funds will eventually hold new mega-listings, so an investor in a total-market fund may get exposure without buying directly.
Volatility around huge, hyped IPOs is common; position size you could stomach losing a chunk of is the usual rule of thumb. This is general information, not advice.

stories.headline: Stocks Surge on Monday: S&P 500 Up 2.35%, Dow Gains 1,104 Points as Oil Slides
stories.deck: The broadest rally in months came as crude fell and volatility eased, even with Nvidia dropping.
paras: All four major benchmarks rose Monday. The S&P 500 closed at 7,549.94, up 2.35% and its best day since April 8. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1,104.02 points, or 2.15%, to 52,389.75. The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.74% to 25,253.14, and the small-cap Russell 2000 jumped 3.15% to 2,840.81. The VIX volatility gauge fell 21.69% to 20.08.

One recap called breadth the day's defining feature, with small caps leading, and tied the move to lower oil and easing volatility without naming a single cause. December crude fell 4.28% to $86.94 a barrel.

Not everything rose. Nvidia dropped 4.27% to $178.67 after its board opened an investigation, while AMD gained 13.26% and Broadcom 8.78%. Tuesday's CPI report, which came in hotter than forecast, is the next test.
money: After a big up day, a scheduled rebalance (rather than a reaction) is the calmer way to keep a stock-bond mix on target.
Small caps outran large caps, a reminder that a total-market or equal-weight fund can behave differently from a large-cap index fund.
Single-day moves of 2% or more are normal in volatile stretches; automatic monthly contributions to a retirement account smooth entry prices.
If a 401(k) has a big company-stock or tech tilt, check how much of a portfolio depends on a handful of names.

sources.t: Stock Market Today, November 9, 2026 (Vista PGlobal)
The Stock Market Today, November 9, 2026 (StockTitan)

stories.headline: Nvidia Board Opens Independent Probe After Reports CEO Jensen Huang Was Targeted by a Foreign Intelligence Effort
stories.deck: The stock fell 4.27% Monday, cutting roughly $192 billion in value since Friday, while the company says it has no sign secrets were compromised.
stories.summary: A committee of independent directors will investigate; NVDA closed at $178.67; earnings are Nov 17.
paras: In a statement dated Nov. 8, Nvidia's board said a committee of independent directors, with outside counsel, will investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it puts U.S. national and economic security first, has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised, and has confidence in Huang, who supports the review and will cooperate.

Nvidia shares closed down 4.27% at $178.67 on Monday; StockTitan put the drop since Friday at about $192 billion in market value, based on 24.1 billion shares. Chip peers mostly rose, with AMD up 13.26% and Broadcom up 8.78%.
Nvidia reports third-quarter results Tuesday, Nov. 17, with a call at 5 p.m. ET, so the probe will be a focus for investors on that call.
money: Because Nvidia is one of the largest stocks in major U.S. index funds, its moves can ripple through a typical retirement account.
Earnings week is a common time for sharp price swings; limit orders can protect against paying a surprise price.
A diversified fund spreads the risk that a single company's governance news hits a portfolio.
Headlines about investigations often move stocks more than the eventual findings do, so decisions made on the first day deserve a second look.

stories.headline: Trump Calls Iran War "Effectively Over" After Meeting Qatar, and Oil Drops to a Three-Month Low
stories.deck: Brent closed near $91, its lowest since August, though ships are still being attacked in the Gulf and the main disputes are unresolved.
stories.summary: Brent about $91.10, lowest close since August; Eurasia Group cut renewed-war odds to 30% from 60%.
paras: After meeting Qatar's prime minister at the White House, President Trump called the war militarily "effectively over," said further strikes may not be needed and said U.S. forces remain ready. Eurasia Group cut its odds of renewed all-out hostilities to 30% from 60%, citing political pressure on Trump after the midterms, according to Bloomberg via Rigzone.
Brent fell to about $91.10, its lowest close since August, though it remains up about 50% this year. Midday Monday, one recap had Brent at $93.44 (down 4.96%) and WTI at $86.65.

The disputes are far from settled. Iran wants the U.S. to lift its naval blockade of Gulf ports and drop sanctions before talks; Washington wants attacks on Hormuz shipping to stop plus nuclear concessions. Iran continues to hit several ships a week on average, Secretary of State Rubio said Sunday that talks had made no progress, and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was targeted Monday, causing a limited fire with no casualties reported.
money: Lower crude can take weeks to show up at the pump; tracking local gas prices with a free app helps you time fill-ups.
Energy stocks and funds tend to fall when peace hopes rise; holding some as a hedge against price spikes is a decision to weigh against your overall mix.
If you drive a lot, fixed-price fuel or fuel-cost savings plans are worth reading closely before signing, since prices have been falling.
Airfares and shipping costs follow fuel with a lag, so booking holiday travel on a price-alert tool can pay off.

sources.t: US Holds Off Strikes after Qatari Mediation (Rigzone/Bloomberg)

stories.headline: Russia-Ukraine Talks Open in Abu Dhabi, the First U.S.-Mediated Round in Nine Months
stories.deck: Both sides arrive with the same sticking points, territory and security guarantees, and Ukrainian officials say not to expect much.
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi talks run Nov 10-11 with U.S. envoys Witkoff and Kushner; big gaps remain on territory and guarantees.
paras: Two days of talks began Tuesday in Abu Dhabi with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner mediating. Rustem Umerov leads Ukraine's team and Vladimir Medinsky leads Russia's, with Russian deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov joining for the first time. A U.S. official described negotiators as cautiously optimistic, and Ukraine's Kyrylo Budanov told CBS he did not expect significant progress.

The gaps are wide. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the rest of Donetsk, with ABC reporting broader demands on four regions, a permanent NATO ban and limits on Ukraine's military. Kyiv wants binding security guarantees and a ceasefire along current lines, and refuses to recognize Russian control of occupied land. Russia is resisting a European role, though France and Germany say they will take part in some form.

ABC also reported that U.S. aid to Ukraine is suspended, and that Trump has not followed through on threatened Russia sanctions and struck a diesel import deal with Putin. Trump says the war will end soon; fighting continued overnight with heavy drone and missile strikes.
money: Peace headlines have repeatedly moved wheat, natural gas and defense stocks in both directions; avoid trading on a single day's news.
A real ceasefire could ease European gas and food prices, which flow through to global inflation over months rather than days.
Defense and energy funds can be volatile around talks; check how much of a diversified fund is already in those sectors before adding more.
Donating to relief groups? Check charity ratings before giving, since scams follow major news events.

sources.t: Russia, Ukraine resume Abu Dhabi talks as major hurdles remain (The New Arab)
Russia, Ukraine and US meet for Abu Dhabi talks as Trump says war can end soon (ABC News)

stories.headline: Correction: The 178 China Tariff Exclusions Did Not Lapse; They Were Extended to Jan. 9
stories.deck: Yesterday we flagged a Nov. 9 expiry. The U.S. had extended the exclusions on Nov. 6, and China announced a two-month pause on a 24% extra tariff.
stories.summary: USTR extended 178 Section 301 exclusions to Jan 9, 2027; China is suspending a 24% extra tariff for two months, keeping 10%.
paras: Yesterday's edition said 178 Section 301 exclusions would lapse overnight. That has been overtaken: Caixin reports that the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative announced on Nov. 6 it was extending them by two months, to Jan. 9, 2027. The list covers 164 industrial and medical product categories and 14 solar equipment categories. The same date applies to the suspension of port fees on Chinese ships and of added tariffs on Chinese-made ship-to-shore cranes.

Caixin also reports that China's customs tariff commission announced Nov. 9 that it would suspend an additional 24% tariff on U.S. goods for two months starting Nov. 10, while keeping a 10% tariff. Caixin's page is paywalled and that detail comes from a summary labeled for reference only, so confirm it before relying on it.

A tariff tracker updated Nov. 3 had listed Nov. 10 as a deadline for deferred 100% tariffs on cranes and chassis and for suspended Chinese rare-earth export controls. The Caixin report covers the cranes; we did not find a source on rare earths today.
money: Importers and small sellers that rely on excluded products get two more months of breathing room, but planning for Jan. 9 costs now beats scrambling later.
Shoppers should expect less sudden price shock on affected industrial, medical and solar equipment before January.
Companies exposed to China trade tend to move sharply on tariff headlines; a long-term holding plan is steadier than reacting to each deadline.
If your work touches imports, check your products' tariff codes against the exclusion list.

sources.t: U.S. Extends Tariff Exclusions for 178 Chinese Product Categories (Caixin)
Trump 2.0 Tariff Tracker, Nov. 3 update (Trade Compliance Resource Hub)

stories.headline: The Money Calendar: CPI Today, Cisco and CoreWeave This Week, Nvidia Nov. 17, Fed Dec. 8-9, Funding Cliff Dec. 11
stories.deck: Dates through early 2027 that can move prices, rates and benefits.
stories.summary: Key dates: Nov 17 Nvidia, Dec 8-9 Fed, Dec 11 funding deadline, Dec 31 Covered California, Jan 1 wage and tariff changes.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. This week: CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials report quarterly results, and Sonos reports Tuesday after the close. Covered California's phone line is closed Wednesday, Nov. 11, for Veterans Day. Nvidia reports Tuesday, Nov. 17. Anthropic's offering was reported able to price as early as the week of Nov. 16, per Renaissance Capital.

December: the Federal Reserve meets Dec. 8-9, federal funding runs out Dec. 11, and the polysilicon tariffs listed in one tracker take effect Dec. 4. Pick a Covered California plan by Dec. 31 for Jan. 1 coverage.

Early 2027: the new Congress is sworn in Jan. 3; California's minimum wage rises to $17.40 and furniture and cabinet tariffs step up on Jan. 1; the China tariff exclusions now run to Jan. 9; and Covered California open enrollment ends Jan. 31.
money: Put the Dec. 31 health-plan deadline on your calendar; waiting until January can leave you without 2027 coverage from Jan. 1.
If you plan to buy furniture or cabinets, buying before Jan. 1 avoids the step-up, though discounts and demand may vary.
Employers and freelancers who pay by the hour can budget for the Jan. 1 wage change now.
Review withholding and retirement contributions before year-end using the 2027 IRS numbers covered below.

stories.headline: Shutdown Clock: Federal Funding Runs Out Dec. 11 and Congress Has Passed Only 3 of 12 Spending Bills
stories.deck: The lame-duck Congress has about a month to pass full-year funding or another stopgap.
stories.summary: Stopgap H.R. 6500 expires Dec 11; the Senate had passed none of the 12 regular spending bills as of Nov 3.
paras: The stopgap funding law, H.R. 6500, keeps most agencies at current-year spending through Dec. 11. The House passed it 370-48 and President Trump signed it Sept. 2. As of Nov. 3, the House had passed three of the 12 regular spending bills and the Senate none. Flood insurance and surface transportation extensions expire around the same date.

Options include a full-year omnibus, a short stopgap into early 2027 or a mix. Most bills need 60 Senate votes. The stopgap also carried SNAP ($107.5 billion) and WIC ($8.2 billion) funding through Dec. 11.

Shutdowns have been frequent: a 43-day shutdown ran from Oct. 1 to Nov. 12, 2025, and a 35-day lapse ran from December 2018 into January 2019. One analysis found the S&P 500 averaged a 0.3% gain during 22 shutdowns since 1976, though another firm found it went essentially nowhere.
money: A lapse can delay federal paychecks, passport and permit processing and some benefits; keeping a cushion of cash for a month is common guidance for federal workers and contractors.
Anyone buying or renewing flood insurance should check that the National Flood Insurance Program is still authorized when the policy is issued.
Historically, stocks have mostly looked past shutdowns, so selling on the headline has often not paid.
SNAP and WIC households should keep an eye on state notices in December about benefit timing.

sources.t: The 11 December Funding Deadline: Shutdown Risk After the Midterms (Multibagg)
US government shutdown threat lifted through Dec. 11 as Trump signs stopgap (Latin Times)

stories.headline: Tariffs by the Calendar: Polysilicon Dec. 4, Furniture and Cabinets Jan. 1, New Probes in Robotics and Wind
stories.deck: A tracker updated Nov. 3 lists what is in force and what steps up next.
stories.summary: Furniture and cabinet tariffs rise Jan 1; polysilicon tariffs start Dec 4; robotics and wind turbine actions opened in late October.
paras: The Nov. 3 tracker shows upholstered wooden furniture at 25% through Dec. 31 and 30% from Jan. 1, and kitchen cabinets and vanities at 25% now and 50% from Jan. 1. Polysilicon tariffs of 10% to 15%, with minimum import prices, start Dec. 4. Pharmaceuticals took effect July 31, with generics exempt.

Initial Section 232 actions came on wind turbines (Oct. 22) and robotics and industrial machinery (Oct. 28), with status reports due in April 2027. Steel, aluminum and copper tariffs now apply to the full value of goods at 25% to 50% and trucks and parts are at 25%. Brazil faces a 25% Section 301 tariff and forced-labor tariffs of 10% to 12.5% began July 24.

The Court of International Trade ruled the Section 122 proclamation invalid on May 7, but there was no universal injunction, so collection continues while the government appeals. For Canada, a 50% Section 338 tariff on motor vehicles, alcohol and dairy took effect Aug. 22.
money: Furniture and cabinet buyers face the biggest scheduled jump on Jan. 1, so a remodel quote taken now may be cheaper than one in January.
Appliance, machinery and solar buyers should expect supply-chain pricing to follow tariff steps with a lag.
Tariff costs are mostly paid by importers first and passed on selectively; comparing prices across retailers beats assuming one is raising more.
Small manufacturers can ask a customs broker whether any products qualify for exclusions or refunds.

sources.t: Trump 2.0 Tariff Tracker, Nov. 3 update (Trade Compliance Resource Hub)

stories.headline: Tariff Refunds: $100 Billion Paid by July 31, About $66 Billion Still Owed, and Consumers Rarely See It
stories.deck: The money goes to importers, and some retailers are passing savings to shoppers while others are selling their claims.
stories.summary: $166 billion total; $100 billion paid as of July 31; about $11.4 billion tied up in a court appeal.
paras: Customs and Border Protection told the Court of International Trade it had paid $100 billion in refunds of the struck-down emergency tariffs as of July 31, out of a $166 billion total, per Supply Chain Dive. Of the $128.68 billion accepted through its CAPE portal, roughly $28.7 billion was accepted but unpaid. About $11.4 billion on finally liquidated entries cannot yet be processed and is tied to a pending Justice Department appeal.

The Supreme Court struck down the tariffs on Feb. 20, 2026, and CAPE launched April 20; refunds generally issue 60 to 90 days after acceptance, per the Nov. 3 tracker. Importers get the money. Amazon reported receiving $600 million.

Amazon and Costco said they would refund some customers, while Walmart, BJ's Wholesale Club and e.l.f. Beauty are using refunds to lower prices. American Eagle and The Children's Place sold their rights to future refunds for quick cash. These figures are as of late July, the latest we found.
money: Check whether stores you shop at have announced customer refund or price-cut programs tied to the tariff money.
Small importers should confirm their entries were filed through CAPE and watch for accepted-but-unpaid status.
Be wary of anyone charging fees to chase refunds without explaining how the CAPE portal process works.
A retailer using refunds to cut prices may signal pricing room on goods you plan to buy.

sources.t: CBP has paid $100B in IEEPA tariff refunds (Supply Chain Dive)

stories.headline: Oil Hits a Three-Month Low, Gold Climbs Above $4,100, and the 30-Year Mortgage Rate Is 7.18%
stories.deck: Commodities and borrowing costs moved in different directions on peace hopes and a softer dollar.
stories.summary: Brent about $91; gold about $4,123; Freddie Mac 30-year at 7.18% (third straight decline).
paras: Brent crude closed near $91.10, its lowest close since August, and December WTI settled at $86.94 on Monday. Gold rose 1.4% to about $4,123 an ounce as the dollar index slipped 0.49% to 101.795. Silver gained 1.75% to $52.85 and natural gas rose 4.7% to $3.139 per million BTU, bucking the energy decline.

Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 7.18% for the week of Nov. 5, down from 7.24% and the third straight weekly decline, but about 0.96 point above a year ago. Mortgage Bankers Association data show purchase applications down 19% from a year earlier and refinancing applications down 60%.
RealEstateNews noted rates are below the roughly 7.5% level of a few weeks ago but buyer activity has not picked up; Freddie Mac publishes its survey weekly.
money: A 0.06-point drop barely changes a monthly payment; shopping at least three lenders for the same loan can save far more than waiting for a small rate move.
Gold at this level is a high price to buy at; if you own it, rebalancing is a decision about your whole portfolio rather than a single price.
Falling crude can lower gasoline and heating costs through the winter if it holds.
If you are considering a refinance, run the break-even: closing costs divided by monthly savings.

stories.headline: Monday Movers: Telos +49%, Greenfire +38% on a Buyout, Ionis -21%, SpaceX Up After NASA Lunar Awards
stories.deck: Raised forecasts and deals drove the biggest gains; guidance cuts and trial data drove the losses.
stories.summary: Telos +48.76%, Greenfire +38.21%, Ionis -21.36%, monday.com -9.10%, Alphabet +1.18%.
paras: Among the biggest gainers Monday were Telos (+48.76%) after raising its 2026 revenue forecast, Greenfire Resources (+38.21%) after Strathcona Resources agreed to buy it, and Delcath Systems (+35.77%) on a higher revenue forecast. Fervo Energy rose 26.09% after third-quarter results.

Decliners included Faeth Therapeutics (-42.49%) after early mid-stage cancer trial results, Janux Therapeutics (-27.62%) after early data, Ionis (-21.36%) after cutting its 2026 Tryngolza sales forecast and monday.com (-9.10%) after forecasting slower fourth-quarter growth.

In large caps, Alphabet rose 1.18% to $288.15 after unveiling two new TPU chips, and SpaceX shares were reported up 5.81% at $142.07 after NASA selected eight companies for a lunar delivery framework with a $10 billion shared contract ceiling.
money: Single-day moves of 20% or more in small caps are common and reverse often; they are a poor basis for allocating savings.
Guidance cuts after earnings can matter more than the quarter just reported.
If you hold a fund, read its top-10 holdings to see which of these names it contains.
Biotech trial results are binary events; position sizes in them are usually kept small.

stories.headline: Deals: Marvell's $115 Billion All-Stock Lumentum Takeover and Strathcona's Greenfire Buyout
stories.deck: The Marvell-Lumentum deal, signed Nov. 2, would not close until the first half of 2028.
stories.summary: Marvell pays 4.5 of its shares per Lumentum share, about $1,132 each and a 23.9% premium.
paras: Marvell agreed on Nov. 2 to buy Lumentum for about $115 billion in an all-stock deal, with each Lumentum share converting into 4.5 Marvell shares. That values Lumentum at about $1,132 a share, a 23.9% premium over its Oct. 28 close, the last trading day before deal speculation. Marvell holders would own about 67% of the combined company and Lumentum holders about 33%.
Closing is expected in the first half of 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approval, so the long timeline leaves room for the deal to change or fail.
On a smaller scale, Greenfire Resources jumped 38.21% Monday after Strathcona Resources agreed to buy it, with shareholder meetings set for January 2027.
money: In stock-for-stock deals, the target's price tracks the buyer's price; Lumentum holders carry Marvell risk until close.
Merger-arbitrage spreads reflect the market's view of deal risk; they are not a free lunch for retail investors.
Index funds that hold both companies will see their stakes merge automatically.
Deals that take years to close tend to attract regulatory scrutiny.

stories.headline: Bitcoin Slips to About $74,500, Down 29% From a Year Ago and 41% Below Its October 2025 Peak
stories.deck: A reported Treasury move against an exchange and delays to crypto legislation have weighed on prices.
stories.summary: Bitcoin $74,549 at 7:30 a.m. ET Nov 9; down 8.8% in a month and 28.8% in a year.
paras: Bitcoin traded at $74,549.48 at 7:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 9, down about 1.7% from the day before, 8.8% from a month earlier and 28.8% from a year earlier, according to Fortune. Its all-time high of $126,198.07 came on Oct. 6, 2025. Ethereum was near $2,118.

The Sunday Guardian reported a recent high near $80,935 and cited a reported U.S. Treasury action against the exchange MEXC, long liquidations, delays to crypto legislation after the midterms and brief spot-ETF outflows as drivers. It described $73,700 to $74,000 as key support. That report is a single article and its figures were not cross-checked.
money: Crypto can fall 8% in a month; money you need within a few years usually does not belong in it.
Dollar-cost averaging a small, fixed amount reduces the risk of a badly timed lump sum.
Taxes: selling at a loss may offset gains elsewhere; keep records of every trade.
Use only exchanges you have verified, since regulatory actions can freeze access.

stories.headline: The Children's Place Files for Bankruptcy and Aims to Sell Itself by Year-End
stories.deck: The retailer started store-closing sales last week, and bids are due in about a month.
stories.summary: Filing came Nov 9 after a leadership shake-up on Nov 6; American Eagle also sold rights to tariff refunds.
paras: The Children's Place filed for bankruptcy on Nov. 9 after starting store-closing sales the previous week, according to Retail Dive. It aims to sell itself by year-end, with bids due in about a month. On Nov. 6, several executives and directors, including the CEO, left and the CFO became principal executive officer.
Supply Chain Dive reported separately that The Children's Place and American Eagle sold their rights to future tariff refunds for quick capital.
money: Gift cards and store credit from a retailer in bankruptcy can lose value; spend them soon or ask whether they will be honored.
Returns policies may tighten during liquidation sales, so check terms before buying.
Before buying a large item on layaway or a deposit, confirm the seller is solvent.
Holiday shopping through a retailer in Chapter 11 carries more risk for prepaid orders.

sources.t: Distressed Retail (Retail Dive)
CBP has paid $100B in IEEPA tariff refunds (Supply Chain Dive)

stories.headline: 2027 Tax Numbers Are Set: Standard Deduction $16,600 Single and $33,200 Joint, Child Credit $2,300
stories.deck: The IRS adjusted brackets for inflation; the new figures generally apply to returns filed in 2028.
stories.summary: 2027 standard deduction $16,600 single, $33,200 joint; top bracket starts at $661,375 single.
paras: The IRS set the 2027 standard deduction at $16,600 for single filers and married filing separately (up $500), $24,925 for heads of household and $33,200 for married couples filing jointly (up $1,000). The 12% bracket starts above $12,800 of taxable income for singles and $25,600 for couples. The 22% bracket starts at $52,025 (single) and $104,050 (joint), and the 37% bracket above $661,375 and $793,650.

The child tax credit is $2,300 per child with up to $1,800 refundable. The Earned Income Tax Credit tops out at $8,496 for three or more children, the health flexible spending account cap is $3,500 and the annual gift exclusion is $20,000.
These apply to income earned in 2027, so they matter for withholding and planning rather than the return you file this spring.
money: Update your W-4 or estimated payments early in 2027 if your income or household changed.
A $3,500 health FSA cap and $350 monthly commuter benefit are use-it-or-lose-it style limits worth budgeting for during open enrollment.
Higher brackets and standard deductions rise with inflation, so a raise that merely matches inflation does not push most people into a higher bracket.
Gifts up to $20,000 per recipient need no gift-tax return.

sources.t: IRS Adjusts Tax Brackets, Standard Deduction for Tax Year 2027 (CPA Practice Advisor)
2027 tax brackets and standard deduction: Full IRS rates (FOX 11 Los Angeles)

stories.headline: California FAIR Plan Rates Rise 29.1% on Average for Policies Renewing Since Oct. 15
stories.deck: The state approved less than the 35.8% the insurer of last resort had requested.
stories.summary: FAIR Plan increase applies to renewals on or after Oct 15; shopping early and adding a companion policy matter.
paras: The California Department of Insurance approved an average 29.1% increase for FAIR Plan policies, the largest in recent history, after the plan requested 35.8%. KQED reports it affects more than 675,000 customers, with some high wildfire-risk homeowners seeing wildfire premiums double while some lower-risk urban Bay Area policyholders may pay less. The new rates apply to policies renewing on or after Oct. 15; earlier renewals keep current pricing until their next renewal.

Coverage Cat, an insurance blog, says the plan covers fire and a few related perils, so most homeowners also need a companion policy; it gives illustrative combined costs of about $4,000 to $6,200 a year for a $500,000 dwelling in a moderate fire zone. It cites losses from the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires and higher reinsurance costs. Statewide premiums are up 84% since 2020, per a Stanford study cited by KQED.
money: Start shopping about 90 days before renewal, ideally through an independent broker who can access both standard and surplus-lines markets.
Document wildfire-hardening work with photos and receipts; some insurers give credit for it.
Right-size coverage to reconstruction cost, not market value, and compare at least three companion quotes.
Do not drop liability or loss-of-use coverage just to save on premium.

sources.t: California FAIR Plan announces 29.1% rate hike (KQED)
California FAIR Plan Rate Hikes in 2026 (Coverage Cat)

stories.headline: California's Minimum Wage Rises to $17.40 on Jan. 1, and the Exempt Salary Floor Hits $72,384
stories.deck: Local ordinances may require more in some cities, including parts of Los Angeles County.
stories.summary: Statewide minimum wage $17.40 from Jan 1, 2027; exempt salary threshold $72,384.
paras: California's statewide minimum wage will be $17.40 an hour on Jan. 1, 2027, the Labor Commissioner's office says; the Department of Finance certified the increase July 31. The minimum salary for exempt workers is $72,384 a year, which is two times the minimum wage for 40-hour weeks over 52 weeks, and exempt workers must also meet duties tests.
Where a city or county sets a higher minimum wage, employers must pay the higher rate, so workers should check their local ordinance.
money: Check your 2027 pay stub in January; a worker paid below $17.40 where no higher local rate applies is owed the difference.
Salaried workers near $72,384 may be reclassified as hourly or get a raise; ask HR early.
Small-business owners can budget for payroll and price changes now.
File a wage claim with the Labor Commissioner if an employer underpays.

sources.t: California minimum wage to rise to $17.40 (California Department of Industrial Relations)
California Minimum Wage Rises to $17.40 an Hour in 2027 (HR Morning)

stories.headline: Covered California Open Enrollment Runs to Jan. 31, With Bigger State Subsidies for Incomes up to 200% of Poverty
stories.deck: Choose a plan by Dec. 31 for coverage that starts Jan. 1; the state boosted its subsidy pool to $300 million.
stories.summary: About 725,000 enrollees pay $100 or less a month; state help reaches incomes up to $31,920 (single).
paras: Open enrollment for 2027 runs from Nov. 1 through Jan. 31, 2027, but plans must be chosen by Dec. 31 to be active on Jan. 1. About 725,000 Californians pay $100 or less a month and 358,000 pay $0. State subsidy funding rises from $190 million in 2026 to $300 million in 2027, and more than 330,000 people will pay less because of it.

State help covers incomes up to 200% of the poverty level, which is $31,920 for an individual and $66,000 for a family of four. More than 1.7 million Californians are enrolled, 12 insurers offer plans and 55% of enrollees will see no premium increase. Federal enhanced tax credits expired last year, costing Californians about $2.5 billion a year.

About 1.1 million uninsured Californians are eligible for coverage: 461,000 for Covered California subsidies and 682,000 for Medi-Cal. Free help is available at (800) 300-1506, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., closed Veterans Day on Nov. 11.
money: Compare plans on CoveredCA.com with subsidies applied; the cheapest-premium plan is not always the cheapest once deductibles are counted.
Check that your doctors and medications are covered before choosing.
If your income is near 200% of poverty, report accurate income to capture state help.
Use a free certified enroller if you are unsure; do not pay for enrollment help.

sources.t: Covered California continues its 2027 open enrollment (Covered California)
Covered California open enrollment begins Nov. 1: what to know for 2027 (NBC Palm Springs)

stories.headline: CalFresh Work Rules Are Live: What to Document, and When
stories.deck: Adults 18 to 64 without a disability or a child under 14 generally need 80 hours a month of work, training or volunteering.
stories.summary: Rules began June 1; current recipients are evaluated at annual renewal; 600,000 Californians could lose benefits.
paras: New CalFresh work requirements took effect June 1, 2026. Adults 18 to 64 with no disability and no dependent child under 14 must show 20 hours a week (80 a month) of work, training or volunteering for benefits beyond three months in a three-year period, per ABC7. Current enrollees are evaluated at their annual renewal, so someone renewing in November faces the test then.

Assemblymember Lashae Sharp-Collins says more than 600,000 Californians face losing benefits, and about 1.5 million people in Los Angeles County receive CalFresh. CBS Sacramento reports that exemptions include people with disabilities and people caring for children under 14, and that many are volunteering at food banks to meet the requirement. In October, part of CalFresh funding shifts to the state, per ABC7.
money: Keep your address, phone and email current with the county so you get every notice.
Start tracking qualifying hours now, with letters or timesheets from the employer or volunteer site.
Ask the county about exemptions before assuming you are subject to the rule.
Food banks and 211 can help bridge a gap if benefits stop.

sources.t: New CalFresh work rules take effect (ABC7)
CalFresh work requirements now in place as 600,000 could lose benefits (CBS Sacramento)

stories.headline: MyFirstEV: Up to $3,500 Off a First Electric Vehicle, Applied at the Dealership, With Nearly 12,000 Buyers So Far
stories.deck: The state has committed $135.5 million and participating automakers match it, for about $271 million.
stories.summary: $3,500 new, $1,750 used; new price cap $50,000, used $25,000; no application after purchase.
paras: California's MyFirstEV program gives first-time zero-emission buyers an instant $3,500 on eligible new vehicles and $1,750 on used ones. New vehicles must carry a recommended price of $50,000 or less; used ones must cost $25,000 or less and be sold through a manufacturer's pre-owned program. Electrive reports no post-purchase application is needed, and nearly 12,000 people have bought through the program since August.

The state committed $135.5 million, matched dollar for dollar by automakers including Ford, GM, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Lucid, Nissan, Rivian, Subaru, Tesla, Toyota and Volvo. KQED says that is enough for about 73,000 vehicles and that low-income residents may qualify for larger incentives under Clean Cars 4 All. Electric vehicles made up 19.1% of California new-car sales in the third quarter.
money: Ask the dealer whether the rebate is applied before you sign, and get it written on the buyer's order.
Compare total cost, including charging at home, rather than the sticker price alone.
Low-income buyers should ask about Clean Cars 4 All, which may be larger.
Funding is finite; waiting may risk the money running out.

sources.t: Nearly 12,000 Californians switch to EVs thanks to MyFirstEV rebate (Electrive)
California announces $3,500 instant rebate for new EV purchases (KQED)

stories.headline: Social Security Rises 3.6% in January, About $75 a Month, but Medicare Premium Will Take a Bite
stories.deck: Part B is projected at $209.50 a month; the final figure is due this month.
stories.summary: COLA 3.6%; projected Part B $209.50 (+$6.60); taxable maximum $192,300.
paras: Social Security benefits rise 3.6% in January 2027, the largest cost-of-living adjustment since 2023, or about $75 a month for the average retired worker. Notices go out starting in early December. The maximum earnings subject to the payroll tax rises to $192,300 from $184,500.

Medicare trustees project the Part B premium rising $6.60 to $209.50 a month, leaving the average retiree about $68.40 a month ahead if that holds; the CMS figure is expected in November. The Part D deductible is projected to rise from $615 to $700. A one-time $90 Part B premium rebate is being paid this month to about 21 million people in traditional Medicare; Medicare Advantage enrollees are not eligible.
money: Watch for the Social Security notice in December to confirm your new amount after the Medicare deduction.
Compare Part D and Medicare Advantage plans during open enrollment, since premiums on some plans are rising.
Higher earners should expect a larger payroll tax base starting in 2027.
Seniors on fixed incomes may qualify for state or county help with utilities and groceries.

sources.t: Social Security's 2027 COLA Rises 3.6%, but Medicare Costs Could Eat Into the Extra $75 a Month (IBTimes UK)
Social Security says retirees will get a 3.6% raise for 2027 (Honolulu Star-Advertiser)

stories.headline: AI Week: OpenAI Ships GPT-6 Cyber, Google Cuts Video Prices 30%, Goldman Limits AI Coding Tools
stories.deck: A roundup of the launches and business moves of the past week, as reported by two AI newsletters.
stories.summary: OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber and Images 2.6; Google Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash; Moonshot open-weights model; Goldman limits coding tools.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. These items come from AI Compass and a weekly AI digest, and the vendor figures were not independently verified. OpenAI rolled out ChatGPT Images 2.6 on Nov. 4 and released GPT-6 Cyber on Nov. 5 to vetted defenders. Google made Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash generally available on Nov. 5, with 720p video pricing cut 30% to $0.07 per second. Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro with open weights, and Meta added realtime voice and avatars.

On the business side, a digest said Goldman Sachs restricted Claude Code and GitHub to its engineering teams, and that OpenAI raised $11 billion at a $1.25 trillion valuation (the digest's own text and its source link disagree on whether that was above or below the target, so treat it as uncertain). AI Compass also noted that Anthropic launched a U.S. beta of Personal Finance in Claude with read-only Plaid connections.
money: Before linking bank accounts to any AI finance tool, read what permissions it gets and use read-only access.
Falling AI video prices mean small businesses can produce ads for less; compare per-second rates.
Free open-weight models can cut costs for developers, but check licenses.
Be skeptical of AI investment tips; most of these valuations are for private companies.

sources.t: AI Compass Weekly, Nov. 2-6 (Ashutosh AI)
Weekly AI Digest, November 9, 2026 (DEV Community)

stories.headline: AI's Electric Bill: Data Centers Blamed for $9.3 Billion of Higher Costs in One Grid, and States Move to Make Them Pay
stories.deck: The House passed a ratepayer bill 417-3, but it stalled in the Senate on a 57-43 vote.
stories.summary: National residential rates are up about 7.3%; the Ratepayer Protection Act passed the House but stalled in the Senate.
paras: Disclosure: this briefing was written by Claude, an AI made by Anthropic. The facts below come from outside reporting. Monitoring Analytics, the PJM grid's market watchdog, found that 70% of last year's increased electricity cost, about $9.3 billion, resulted from data center demand, according to Power Engineering. Oregon, New Jersey, Indiana and Pennsylvania have taken steps toward special data center rates or studies, and at least a dozen states are exploring ways to make data centers pay more of transmission costs. Some officials blame tight supply and aging equipment instead.

A report published Oct. 2 says utilities requested $18.6 billion in rate increases in the first half of 2026 and national residential rates are up roughly 7.3% from a year earlier. The Ratepayer Protection Act passed the House 417-3 on Sept. 16, and a Senate cloture vote stalled 57-43 on Sept. 30. The report says Microsoft and Anthropic have pledged to cover their own electricity costs. Experts caution it is hard to isolate the data center share.
money: Check your utility's rate-case filings; public comment periods can influence what customers pay.
Time-of-use rates and efficiency upgrades can offset higher bills.
Ask your representative where they stand on the Ratepayer Protection Act.
Home solar and battery quotes are worth comparing when rates are rising.

sources.t: As electric bills rise, evidence mounts that data centers share blame (Power Engineering)
AI data center boom is pushing up Americans' electricity bills (Political.org)
